Number of waves per second and the length of one wave.

Maximum displacement from the rest position; relates to energy.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Waves, Photons & Astronomy — a core area of A-Level Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Waves, Photons & Astronomy brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Waves, Photons & Astronomy.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: E = hf tells us that a photon's energy is proportional to its:
options: Brightness
Frequency
Wavelength
Amplitude

mcqs.q: Light entering glass from air bends towards the normal because:
options: Gravity pulls the ray downwards.
It slows down in the optically denser medium.
It speeds up in the glass.
Its frequency falls to zero.

mcqs.q: The redshift of distant galaxies suggests that:
options: They are hotter than the Sun.
They are approaching us.
Light loses its colour with age.
They are receding from us, consistent with an expanding universe.

mcqs.q: According to Hubble's law, a galaxy twice as far away recedes:
options: Half as fast
At the same speed
Four times as fast
Twice as fast

mcqs.q: Does brighter light carry more energy per photon?
options: Yes — brighter light has more energetic photons.
Yes — glass absorbs half of the frequency.
Yes — intensity increases the speed of the photons.
No — photon energy depends only on frequency (E = hf); greater intensity means more photons.

mcqs.q: When light slows down entering glass, does its frequency decrease?
options: Yes — after a short warming-up delay.
Yes — glass absorbs half of the frequency.
Yes — slower light must oscillate more slowly.
No — frequency is unchanged; the wavelength shortens as the speed drops.

mcqs.q: Below the threshold frequency, can very bright light release photoelectrons?
options: Yes — glass absorbs half of the frequency.
Yes — enough intensity will eventually free the electrons.
No — each photon still has too little energy to overcome the work function, however many photons arrive.
Yes — after a short warming-up delay.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Photon”?
options: Wave speed equals frequency multiplied by wavelength: v = fλ.
The stretching of light from receding sources to longer wavelengths; distant galaxies show redshift, evidence for an expanding universe.
A discrete packet (quantum) of electromagnetic energy with energy E = hf.
The change in direction of a wave as it passes between media in which it travels at different speeds.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Hubble's law”?
options: Wave speed equals frequency multiplied by wavelength: v = fλ.
The stretching of light from receding sources to longer wavelengths; distant galaxies show redshift, evidence for an expanding universe.
The change in direction of a wave as it passes between media in which it travels at different speeds.
The recession speed of a galaxy is proportional to its distance from us: v = H₀d.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Refraction”?
options: Wave speed equals frequency multiplied by wavelength: v = fλ.
The stretching of light from receding sources to longer wavelengths; distant galaxies show redshift, evidence for an expanding universe.
The recession speed of a galaxy is proportional to its distance from us: v = H₀d.
The change in direction of a wave as it passes between media in which it travels at different speeds.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Wave equation”?
options: The emission of electrons from a metal surface when light above a threshold frequency strikes it.
The recession speed of a galaxy is proportional to its distance from us: v = H₀d.
Wave speed equals frequency multiplied by wavelength: v = fλ.
The change in direction of a wave as it passes between media in which it travels at different speeds.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Redshift”?
options: The change in direction of a wave as it passes between media in which it travels at different speeds.
A discrete packet (quantum) of electromagnetic energy with energy E = hf.
The emission of electrons from a metal surface when light above a threshold frequency strikes it.
The stretching of light from receding sources to longer wavelengths; distant galaxies show redshift, evidence for an expanding universe.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Photoelectric effect”?
options: The recession speed of a galaxy is proportional to its distance from us: v = H₀d.
The emission of electrons from a metal surface when light above a threshold frequency strikes it.
The change in direction of a wave as it passes between media in which it travels at different speeds.
The stretching of light from receding sources to longer wavelengths; distant galaxies show redshift, evidence for an expanding universe.

mcqs.q: Using v = fλ, what is the frequency of a sound wave of wavelength 0.5 m travelling at 340 m/s?
options: 680 Hz
170 Hz
